title: Al-Khwarizmi and the Origin of the Word "Algebra"
explainer: The word 'algebra' comes from al-jabr, a term from the title of a 9th-century treatise written in Baghdad by the mathematician Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi, who worked at the House of Wisdom. His book gave systematic methods for solving linear and quadratic equations — written out entirely in words, since symbolic notation like the 'x' and '=' used in this lesson didn't exist yet. His own name, Latinized, is also where the word 'algorithm' comes from.

title: Euler and the Invention of f(x) Notation
explainer: The f(x) notation this lesson uses for functions wasn't always standard — for a long time mathematicians described functions in words or as properties attached to a specific curve. The Swiss mathematician Leonhard Euler introduced the modern f(x) symbol around the 1730s, and it caught on because it let mathematicians treat 'a function' as a single algebraic object you could manipulate directly, rather than re-deriving it from a picture of a curve each time.
